case_title: MUKESH & ANR. v. STATE FOR NCT OF DELHI & ORS.
evidence_type: Medical, dying declaration, eyewitness, circumstantial, scientific
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal, barbaric, diabolic nature of the crime; insertion of iron rod in the private parts of the victim; throwing the victim out of the bus in a vegetative state; causing sepsis and death; coldness and cruelty in the manner of the crime; threat to society; shocking the collective conscience of society
mitigating_circumstances: Family circumstances, young age, absence of criminal antecedents, conduct in jail, likelihood of reformation
neutral_facts: The accused, a group of six men, committed a series of violent acts against a female victim and her friend while they were on a bus. The victim and her friend were picked up from a bus stand with the intent to commit a crime. The accused formed an agreement to commit heinous offences against the victim. They subjected the victim to brutal sexual assault, including the insertion of an iron rod into her private parts, causing severe internal injuries. The victim was then thrown out of the moving bus in a vegetative state, leading to her death due to sepsis. The accused also committed similar acts against the victim's friend. The prosecution presented evidence including medical reports, dying declarations, eyewitness accounts, and scientific evidence such as DNA and odontology reports. The accused were found guilty of rape, criminal conspiracy, and murder.
